subject: On-Prem release surge playbook: stability sprint, gating & rollback rehearsal
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, kevin.lu@acme.com, ops-support@colossus.io
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-Prem release surge playbook: stability sprint, gating & rollback rehearsal

Team —

We need a compact, operational plan for the on-prem (VPC) release that will cover: a short stability sprint prior to the pinset, a staggered surge release (low->med->full), and an explicit rollback rehearsal. Acme is asking for a concrete blackout window and the runbook we will follow for rollbacks/fast-fail.

Key asks from me for Monday:
- A proposed maintenance window (UTC) that balances Acme's preference and our infra availability.
- A canary-selection plan (how many hosts/regions, traffic %).
- A short rollback rehearsal checklist that our SREs can run ahead of the weekend.
- Any vendor constraints (Colossus runtime/drivers) and a graceful fallback path to hosted inference if on-prem fails.

I've attached a draft patch matrix (2027.05.patch-matrix.xlsx) with model/service versions and the proposed pin targets. Please review and add gating criteria as comments in the sheet.

I want a dry-run of the rollback checklist inside the rehearsal window, not just a post-mortem. If we can agree on timings and triggers by EOD Tuesday, I'll coordinate change-order and customer comms.

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Product Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: 2027.05.patch-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, kevin.lu@acme.com
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-Prem release surge playbook: stability sprint, gating & rollback rehearsal

Evelyn —

Thanks for the primer. Quick technical notes and proposed sequence:

1) Pin targets & compatibility
- Controller: 2.3.1 (pin)
- Serving runtime: 7.4.x -> upgrade to 7.4.3 (drivers pinned)
- Quantization lib: qlib-1.9 (no runtime change)

We should avoid a full fleet bounce. My recommendation: staged image rollout in three steps: 1) infra-only control plane nodes (sanity checks), 2) 5% canary serving hosts (observe 6 hours), 3) 25% ramp, 4) full ramp. Each ramp step requires explicit OK from SRE channel.

2) Rollback gating criteria (high level)
- Token-latency 99th percentile > baseline + 120ms for 15m
- Error rate (5xx) > 0.8% sustained for 10m
- KV cache miss spike > 3x baseline for 30m
- Telemetry anomaly: model output regression (model-eval hooks)

3) Rehearsal / dry-run
- We will rehearse a forced canary rollback on Wed (rehearsal window below). Steps: drain traffic from canary hosts, revert image to previous, verify KV cache warm, and run smoke suite (10 prompts per model). This should be scripted and timed.

4) Fallback options
- If rollback fails or systemic regressions appear, failover to hosted model endpoint (region-specific). Documented flow and API keys prepared.

Attachments: I added a canary-selection CSV with a recommended host list and ramp percentages. Also left comments in the patch matrix.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Lead Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: canary-selection.csv (CSV)]

From: Kevin Lu <kevin.lu@acme.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, ops-support@colossus.io
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-Prem release surge playbook: stability sprint, gating & rollback rehearsal

Evelyn / team —

Thanks for the detailed plan. Acme's operations team prefers a maintenance window during our low-traffic period: May 20 02:00–06:00 UTC. That works for us provided there is a clear rollback SLA and a pre-signed change order. Our security team will want the rehearsal to include evidence of KV cache integrity and audit logs for token routing.

Two small asks: could you include an optional shorter window (May 19 23:00–01:00 UTC) for a limited rehearsal only (non-disruptive) and confirm that the hosted fallback will route traffic within 2 minutes of a declared failover?

Cc'ing Colossus ops to confirm driver compatibility notes.

Best,
Kevin Lu
Director, Platform Engineering — Acme Cloud
kevin.lu@acme.com

[Procurement contact: procurement@acme.com]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, kevin.lu@acme.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-Prem release surge playbook: stability sprint, gating & rollback rehearsal

All —

I sketched a short rehearsal checklist (see attached) and a proposed canary grouping. High-level:

- Rehearsal (non-disruptive): May 19 23:30–00:30 UTC — run through the script on canary hosts, validate log collection, and exercise the host revert path. No traffic changes.
- Full maintenance: May 20 02:00–06:00 UTC — staged rollout and 6h canary observation before wider ramp.

Canary grouping rules (from canary-selection.csv):
- Pick hosts across two AZs, avoid hosts with >60% CPU historically, prefer hosts with recent successful health-checks.
- Traffic split: 5% -> 25% -> 100% (per Dev's sequence).

Rollback rehearsal steps (short):
1) Isolate canary (announce on SRE channel).
2) Drain new-worker traffic, verify connection close within 30s.
3) Apply revert image, restart service, run KV-warmup script.
4) Run smoke-suite (included in checklist).
5) Validate telemetry, sign-off.

I'll lead the rehearsal and will coordinate with Acme for the optional May 19 window if Kevin confirms. Attached: stability-sprint-rehearsal-checklist.pdf

—Monica
Monica Patel
Cloud Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: stability-sprint-rehearsal-checklist.pdf (PDF)]
